title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Pool and spa servicing
audience: Pool and spa servicing operators, including solo operators, starting or growing a residential or holiday-let pool and spa service.
learningOutcomes: Write a pool or spa service offer with a clear promised outcome, time frame and conditions
Identify the friction and risk a pool owner carries, and reduce them
Price the offer on value and cost, not only time

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: 'I will service your pool' is a service. 'I will test and balance the water on every visit, clean the walls, skimmer and filter basket, send you the readings and a photo the same day, and come back at no charge if a reading is outside the range we agreed' is an offer. The pool owner buys a clear-water result they can see, and the certainty that someone is checking it.

instruction.heading: The five parts of an offer
instruction.body: Name the outcome, such as the readings inside the range agreed with the client, a clean filter and no visible algae at the next visit. Set the time frame, such as a fortnightly or monthly visit on a stated day. List what the client must do, such as giving access, keeping the pump timer set and telling you when the cover is used or the spa is heavily used. Give the certainty, which is the test log and photos. Name the risk you carry, which is the return visit. Put scope and exclusions in writing: whether chemicals are supplied, whether repairs are quoted separately, and whether a barrier inspection is excluded. A written quote can become binding once it is accepted, so the exclusions protect both sides (business.gov.au, 1 August 2025).

instruction.heading: Reducing friction
instruction.body: Fix the visit day. Keep the gate code or key-safe details in a secure note, not in the quote. Send one shared test log that the client can read on a phone. Give the client one way to pay and one way to change a visit. Fewer steps and fewer decisions for the client usually support a higher price, because the client is paying for convenience and reliability.

instruction.heading: Guarantees and claims
instruction.body: A guarantee must be something you can deliver and afford. Consumer guarantees apply to services, and a 'no refunds' line does not override a customer's rights for services. A written workmanship warranty is an optional promise that sits on top of those rights (business.gov.au, 27 May 2025). Consumer Victoria's guidance says services must be done with due care and skill, but it does not set a fix-window length, so choose a window you can keep and state it in the offer. Do not promise a water-quality result that depends on bather load, weather or the client's own chemical use. Guarantee the visit, the test and the return visit instead. Any measured claim, such as a clarity figure, needs your own readings behind it.

instruction.heading: Pricing on value
instruction.body: Price from the outcome and the risk, then check the price against cost and time. A premium is justified when the client can see the test log, the reliable visit and the time saved. A Melbourne vendor cost guide puts a typical fortnightly service at about $220 a month, with chemicals extra, and a chemistry-only visit at $84 to $190 (What's The Damage?, updated November 2026). That is one vendor's figure for one city, not a market rate, so use it only to check your own prices. Good-better-best packages step up in price, with each level adding something the client can see, such as a filter clean or a monthly equipment check (Jobber Academy, updated 8 October 2024). Show one clear total and say whether GST is included, as the Western Australian guidance asks (WA Consumer Protection, 4 September 2026).

procedure: Write the outcome in one sentence a pool owner would repeat, such as 'balanced water and a clean filter at every visit'.
Set a visit interval you have checked against your own visit records, and record how often you meet it.
List what the client must do, such as giving access and keeping the pump timer set, and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element: the test log, the photos and a sign-off.
Decide the return-visit promise and check that you can afford the time it takes.
Price from value, then check the package price against your cost and time, and show chemicals as a separate line or state that they are included.

workedExamples.situation: A pool operator in Melbourne charges by the visit and has no written scope. Clients ask why a cheaper competitor's fortnightly quote looks similar. The vendor cost guide's typical fortnightly figure is about $220 a month with chemicals extra (vendor source, updated November 2026).
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Rewrite the offer as a package, and decide how to present chemicals and set the package price.
workedExamples.reasoning: The operator writes a fixed fortnightly package that includes the test, the balance, the skimmer and filter check, a shared test log and a return visit for any out-of-range reading. Chemicals appear as a separate line, so the client can compare like with like. The operator sets the package price from their own cost per visit and their margin, and uses the vendor's typical figure only as a sense check. If the operator's price is above that figure, the offer must show the test log and the return visit clearly enough to justify the difference.

equipmentAndPpe: Test kit or digital tester, calibrated and checked against the manufacturer's instructions

commonErrors.error: Guaranteeing a water result that depends on bather load, weather or the client's own chemical use
commonErrors.prevention: Guarantee only what you control: the visit, the test, the return visit and your own workmanship.

commonErrors.error: Stating a clarity or chemistry result you have not measured
commonErrors.prevention: Use only readings from your own test log, and state the number of visits behind any claim.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority. Check your state's rules before acting.

Pool barrier inspection and certificate rules are state-based and differ between states. Victoria, New South Wales and Queensland each set their own rules. Do not describe or offer a barrier certificate unless the rule in that state allows it. Check the rule for each state you work in.

Chemical storage and dangerous-goods rules are also state-based. The WorkSafe WA guidance cited in this course applies in Western Australia only. Check the rule in your own state before you publish any chemical handling statement in an offer.

qualityStandard: Offer and pricing decisions are written down and checked against cost and time.
Every package shows its visit interval, what is included, what is excluded and how readings are recorded.
documentationEvidence: Written offer or plan, a sample test log, the evidence collected, and the decision made.
summary: A good pool offer promises a water result the operator controls, a fixed visit interval, a shared test log and a fair return visit.
Higher rates follow from a visible test log and reliable visits, not from longer hours.

sourceReferences: business.gov.au, 'Prepare quotes', https://business.gov.au/people/contractors/prepare-quotes, last updated 1 August 2025. Supports: a written quote becomes binding once accepted; a quote should recover cost and add a margin.

Consumer Victoria, 'Services not done with due care and skill', https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/products-and-services/problem-with-a-service/services-not-done-with-due-care-and-skill, last updated 13 October 2023. Supports: due care and skill; the page sets no fix-window length.
ACCC, 'Setting prices: what's allowed', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/pricing/setting-prices-whats-allowed, last modified 15 July 2026. Supports: misleading price statements are prohibited.

WA Consumer Protection, 'Estimates, quotes and deposits', https://www.consumerprotection.wa.gov.au/estimates-quotes-and-deposits, last updated 4 September 2026. Western Australia only. Supports: show the total including GST and whether GST is included.

Jobber Academy, 'Good, Better, Best Pricing Examples', https://getjobber.com/academy/good-better-best-pricing-examples/, published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024. Older source. Supports: stepped packages.

Vendor source (lead generation). Supports: fortnightly service at $135 to $315 a month, typically about $220, chemicals extra; chemistry-only visit $84 to $190.

WorkSafe WA, 'Pool and spa chemicals', https://www.worksafe.wa.gov.au/system/files/documents/2025-12/DGS_PO_Pool-and-spa-chemicals.pdf, undated (file path suggests December 2025). Western Australia only. Supports: incompatible pool chemicals must be kept apart; mixing them can release chlorine gas.

Gap: no pool or spa trade-body source (for example SPASA) was reached. No source was found on pool-specific guarantee or warranty norms. Weekly and monthly plan prices with a stated figure were not found.
